The pick relied heavily on a wrestling-control path rather than multiple independent ways to win.

post_fight.why_pick_lost: Phillips landed takedowns and accumulated control, but created too little effective offense from top position while Jourdain clearly won the striking and damage exchanges.

lesson.summary: When the model likes a plus-money wrestler but confidence is weak and ELO does not confirm, require evidence that control converts into damage, dominant round-winning top time, or real submission threat.
lesson.future_review_rule: Downgrade similar underdogs when their path is mainly takedowns/control and the opponent has enough volume or damage equity to win rounds anyway.

review_notes: This should be treated as a fragile value spot rather than a clean dog bet.
Future comparisons should look for other underdogs with low confidence, mild ELO disagreement, and a control-first win condition.

event_name: UFC Fight Night: Allen vs. Costa

pre_fight.core_win_condition: Costa needed his recent-form momentum and all-around activity to overcome Allen's veteran efficiency and defensive discipline.
known_concerns: The model edge was large, but the confidence band still sat in the weak range.
Costa's apparent ELO support was inflated by an extremely thin sidecar history rather than a stable long-run sample.
Allen had the stronger proven class and experience profile against harder opposition.
Costa trailed on several efficiency and anti-control axes even before the fight.

post_fight.why_pick_lost: Allen outclassed Costa in the most reliable scoring areas: cleaner striking, perfect takedown conversion, meaningful top damage, and sustained control. Costa produced volume but not efficient or round-winning offense.

lesson.summary: Do not treat a large ELO edge as trustworthy when it comes from an unstable fighter history. When a live dog still grades poorly in confidence and loses the veteran-efficiency comparison, the apparent value may be synthetic rather than durable.
lesson.future_review_rule: Downgrade similar dogs when ELO support is based on a tiny sample, the edge remains low-confidence, and the favorite owns the stronger class, efficiency, and control-denial profile.

review_notes: This looks more like a model blind spot than a robbery or variance-heavy loss.
Future comparisons should group underdogs with unstable ELO support and hot-form momentum against proven veterans.

pre_fight.core_win_condition: Tokkos needed his projected efficiency and grappling upside to overwhelm a market that was pricing him like a clear underdog.
known_concerns: Both fighters were operating on only three UFC fights and trait confidence was just 0.4 on each side.
The model confidence was high despite the matchup being built from a very small sample.
Tokkos had strong headline grappling upside, but his anti-control and scramble metrics were dramatically worse than Erslan's.
Tokkos' takedown path depended on 2.87 takedowns per 15 minutes against an opponent with 70% takedown defense.
supporting_context: Broad historical buckets supported the pick shape: model_pick_lower_elo and underdog_elo_against were both profitable patterns.
Similar market-profile and ELO-gap examples were also favorable, which made the pick look more trustworthy than the underlying fighter samples justified.

post_fight.why_pick_lost: Tokkos' projected grappling path failed completely. He went 0 of 6 on takedowns, got controlled for most of the fight, and his higher significant-strike count turned into low-value volume while Erslan won the cleaner, fuller scoring exchanges.

lesson.summary: High-confidence underdog signals are not trustworthy when they are built on tiny UFC samples and a grappling case that lacks anti-control and scramble support. This was a model miss driven by overconfidence in unstable data.
lesson.future_review_rule: Downgrade similar dogs when the model shows strong confidence off a tiny sample, especially if the pick's main path is wrestling/grappling but the anti-control and scramble support are weak.

review_notes: This was not an obvious fade because the broad historical buckets supported the price shape.
The deeper warning lived inside the unstable sample size and the mismatch between Tokkos' grappling promise and his poor anti-control/scramble profile.

pre_fight.core_win_condition: Pimblett needed cardio, grappling threat, and opportunistic finishing to overcome Gaethje's veteran striking pressure, ELO edge, and damage profile.
known_concerns: ELO materially disagreed with the expensive favorite: Gaethje 1468 vs Pimblett 1404, with ELO implying only about 40.9% for Pimblett.
The favorite price required Pimblett to justify a high win probability while facing a much more experienced elite lightweight.
Pimblett's support was concentrated in cardio, grappling threat, and recent form, while Gaethje owned the experience and striking-pressure lanes.
Pimblett trailed on anti-control and striking pressure, creating risk that the grappling/cardio thesis would not translate into round-winning control.
supporting_context: MCP model made Pimblett a 72.3% pick with a confidence score of 8 and a small positive edge versus the market.
Deterministic filter gave Pimblett a validated cardio advantage of +30.8 but also flagged ELO against the pick.
Trait examples matching Pimblett's grappling/cardio/recent-form profile were 6-2, but the ROI was slightly negative at -3.1%, suggesting expensive favorite pricing could erase the apparent edge.

Similar market comps were 6-2 with +7.5% ROI and similar ELO-gap comps were 7-1 with +31.8% ROI, so the surface historical buckets looked supportive even though the fighter-specific ELO/class warning was strong.

post_fight.why_pick_lost: Pimblett won volume but failed to make the grappling/cardio thesis score. He went 0 of 5 on takedowns with no submission attempts or ground strikes, while Gaethje landed the cleaner, higher-impact offense, scored two knockdowns, went 3 of 3 on takedowns, and controlled nearly six minutes.

lesson.summary: Do not let a high model-confidence favorite override a material ELO/class warning when the favorite's thesis depends on grappling/cardio conversion against a proven veteran striker. Expensive favorites with ELO against them need proof that the main path creates actual control, damage, or submission threat.
lesson.future_review_rule: Downgrade similar favorites when ELO disagrees by 50+ points, the opponent has a major experience/striking-pressure edge, and the favorite's positive context is concentrated in grappling or cardio without strong anti-control support.

review_notes: This was not a market-resistance case because the market also favored Pimblett; the fragility came from model/market agreement against ELO and class context.

Future comparisons should look for expensive favorites with high confidence, ELO against the pick, strong cardio/grappling deltas, and an opponent who can punish failed takedowns with damage or control.

pre_fight.odds_note: User reported Buckley was +150 when bet; MCP app odds lookup also had a later/alternate market snapshot with Buckley priced as the favorite.
pre_fight.core_win_condition: Buckley needed his striking pressure, power, and finishing upside to stay upright long enough to punish Brady before Brady's wrestling and top-control game took over.
known_concerns: The model edge at +150 was large, but confidence was still weak at score 2.
ELO disagreed with the pick by 53 points: Brady 1481 vs Buckley 1428.

Buckley had major negative trait deltas in the exact anti-wrestling areas needed for this matchup: cardio -23.5, offensive control -52.6, grappling threat -52.5, anti-control -28.3, and scramble -43.6.
The pick's support was concentrated in experience, striking pressure, and finishing threat, creating a narrower KO/striking-upside path against a dominant grappler.
supporting_context: MCP model made Buckley a 53.6% pick, which looked attractive at +150 because the bet price only required about 40.0% before vig.
Buckley had positive deltas in experience (+40.0), striking pressure (+18.8), finishing threat (+12.9), and a slight recent-form edge.

Similar market-shape comps for the -210 app-odds snapshot were positive, but nearest ELO-gap examples were 2-3 with -36.0% ROI, highlighting that the ELO/trait shape was the more relevant warning lane.

post_fight.why_pick_lost: Buckley's striking and finishing upside never entered the fight because Brady controlled the geography. Brady repeatedly took him down, held long top-control stretches, and produced almost all meaningful offense while Buckley generated almost nothing from distance or underneath.

lesson.summary: A plus-money model edge can still be fragile when the pick's upside is mostly striking/finishing and the opponent owns overwhelming grappling, control, scramble, cardio, and ELO advantages. This should have been treated as a model-value spot that needed a context veto or severe stake reduction.
lesson.future_review_rule: Downgrade similar dogs even with positive model edge when confidence is weak, ELO is against the pick by 50+ points, and the opponent has large grappling/control/cardio/scramble advantages that can erase the pick's striking path.

review_notes: This is a useful historical example because the bet price (+150) made Buckley look like a strong model-edge dog, but the context packet showed the exact losing script.
Future comparisons should search for low-confidence plus-money model picks with ELO against them and severe control/grappling/cardio disadvantages versus a proven wrestler.

pre_fight.core_win_condition: Carpenter needed his projected grappling, offensive control, and scramble advantages to convert takedowns into sustained control or submission threat before Ochoa's striking volume could take over.
known_concerns: Both fighters had very small UFC samples: Carpenter four pre-fight UFC fights and Ochoa three.
Carpenter's model support was highly concentrated in grappling/control traits rather than broad all-phase dominance.
Ochoa had the clear striking-pressure lane, with Carpenter at -38.6 in striking pressure versus Ochoa.
Carpenter's ELO was slightly lower than Ochoa's, and his sidecar ELO history was thin.
supporting_context: MCP model made Carpenter a 67.2% pick at +160, a massive +30.2 point raw edge versus the vig-normalized market.
Carpenter's pre-fight trait deltas were very strong in grappling threat (+63.2), offensive control (+60.6), scramble (+41.5), anti-control (+9.2), and recent form (+5.8).
Trait-match examples with similar grappling/control/scramble advantages were 5-1 with +13.1% ROI.
Similar market-shape examples were 4-1 with +113.6% ROI, and similar ELO/edge examples were 4-1 with +102.0% ROI, making the surface historical evidence look very supportive.

post_fight.why_pick_lost: The projected grappling edge did not convert. Carpenter went only 1 of 7 on takedowns, created almost no control separation, and was badly outstruck by Ochoa's volume and efficiency across three rounds.

lesson.summary: Large plus-money model edges built on small-sample grappling projections can be fragile when the opponent has a clear striking-volume path and enough defensive resistance to keep control from accumulating. Carpenter was a valid model bet at +160, but the context needed a small-sample grappling-conversion warning.
lesson.future_review_rule: Downgrade or stake-reduce similar dogs when the edge is huge but the UFC sample is tiny, the pick's advantage is concentrated in grappling/control, and the opponent owns the striking-pressure lane.

review_notes: This was not a bad price at +160; it was a model-path failure where the projected wrestling did not materialize.
Future comparisons should search for high-confidence plus-money dogs with tiny samples, major grappling/control deltas, and opponents with large striking-pressure advantages.

pre_fight.odds_note: No market odds were found in MCP for this historical review, so the pre-fight analysis defaulted market probabilities to 50/50.
pre_fight.core_win_condition: Bannon needed her cleaner surface profile, ELO, recent form, striking pressure, and finishing-threat advantages to hold up without being trapped underneath Caliari's wrestling and top-control path.
known_concerns: This was a thin-data WMMA fight: Caliari had only two prior UFC fights and trait confidence 0.2, while Bannon had four prior UFC fights and trait confidence 0.6.
Bannon's model support came with weak control-denial signals: offensive control -47.0, grappling threat -15.8, anti-control -21.5, and scramble -8.9 versus Caliari.
Caliari was below the 48% model-support threshold at 41.8%, but her path was specific and live if she could force takedowns and top position.
WMMA low-sample fights should be treated cautiously when the model side has poor anti-control and scramble support.
supporting_context: MCP model made Bannon a 58.2% pick with confidence score 4 and a default 8.2-point edge versus 50/50 because odds were unavailable.
Bannon had pre-fight advantages in ELO (+148), recent form (+58.8), experience (+13.3), striking pressure (+15.2), striking efficiency (+11.2), and finishing threat (+39.5).
The negative context lived in the grappling/control deltas: Bannon trailed badly in offensive control, grappling threat, anti-control, and scramble.

post_fight.why_pick_lost: Bannon produced activity, but Caliari dictated the grappling phases. Caliari landed four takedowns, banked over nine minutes of control, and finished with an arm-triangle after turning top position into a decisive submission threat.

lesson.summary: In thin-data WMMA fights, do not trust a moderate model edge and ELO advantage when the model side is weak in anti-control, scramble, and grappling resistance. A below-threshold opponent can still be a dangerous context veto if her single clear path is takedown-to-control and the favorite lacks control-denial support.
lesson.future_review_rule: Downgrade or stake-reduce similar WMMA model picks when the sample is thin, odds are not strongly favorable, and the pick trails materially in anti-control, scramble, and grappling/control traits.

review_notes: This is not a case to bet the sub-48% opponent under the current rule; it is a case to avoid or reduce exposure on the model side.

Future comparisons should search for WMMA fights with low fighter samples, model-side ELO/form advantages, but severe anti-control/scramble deficits against an opponent with a live wrestling-control path.
